content: LEKTI, also referred to as serine protease inhibitor Kazal-type 5 (SPINK5), is a protein encoded by the SPINK5 gene in humans. LEKTI is a large, multidomain serine protease inhibitor that is expressed in stratified epithelial tissues. It is composed of 15 domains, which are cleaved into smaller, functional fragments by the protease furin. Among these domains, only domains 2 and 15 contain six evenly spaced cysteine residues, which are responsible for forming three intramolecular disulfide bonds characteristic of Kazal-type inhibitors. The remaining domains contain four cysteine residues. These disulfide bonds stabilize the protein into a rigid conformation, enabling it to interact with target proteases through an extended beta-sheet structure. Most domains, except for domains 1, 2, and 15, have an arginine residue at the P1 position, suggesting that trypsin-like proteases are the primary targets of LEKTI. In the epidermis, LEKTI is involved in regulating desquamation, the process of shedding corneocytes, by selectively inhibiting the proteases KLK5, KLK7, and KLK14. Recombinant full-length LEKTI has been shown to inhibit exogenous serine proteases such as trypsin, plasmin, subtilisin A, cathepsin G, and human neutrophil elastase. LEKTI is also thought to play a role in skin and hair morphogenesis, as well as in providing anti-inflammatory and/or antimicrobial protection to mucosal epithelial surfaces. The SPINK5 gene belongs to a family of genes located on chromosome 5q32, which encode inhibitors of serine proteases. This family includes other epidermal proteins such as SPINK6 and LEKTI-2 (SPINK9). The SPINK5 gene spans 61 kilobases and contains 33 exons. Alternative processing of SPINK5 results in the production of three distinct gene products, which have been identified in differentiated keratinocytes. Mutations in the SPINK5 gene can lead to Netherton syndrome, a genetic disorder characterized by ichthyosis (scaly skin), defective cornification (abnormal skin barrier formation), and atopy (a predisposition to allergic conditions).
